basis: Defined as intrinsic asthma with exercise-triggered airway narrowing; immune-mediated airway inflammation supports the mechanism axis.

decisions.infectious_immune: primary: the supplied definition explicitly classifies this as intrinsic asthma, an immune-mediated inflammatory airway disease.

basis: Congenital facial paralysis with variable hearing loss defines the syndrome; persistent failure of eyelid closure in 3/3 constitutes ocular functional impairment.

decisions.ocular: involved: lagophthalmos in 3/3 represents persistent loss of eyelid closure function; eyelids are explicitly included in the ocular axis.

basis: Scalp aplasia and limb defects define AOS; brain/developmental damage and visual impairment each reported in 1/2. Optic atrophy alone is 3/12; small samples limit certainty.

decisions.ocular: involved: visual impairment is reported in 1/2 (50%), supporting functional involvement; optic atrophy at 3/12 (25%) alone would not qualify.

basis: Macrophage storage defines splenic/marrow disease; hepatic infiltration 80-99% and skeletal damage 30-79%. Neurologic findings concentrate in neuronopathic subtypes and are omitted under the cap.

decisions.haematologic: primary: Gaucher disease is a macrophage storage disease with defining splenic/marrow involvement and cytopenias, satisfying the blood-cell/marrow mechanism rule.

basis: Open spinal dysraphism affects spinal neural tissue and vertebral closure. Neurogenic bladder occurs in roughly 80-90% but is separately diagnosed; direct urinary tract damage is not established at 30%.

decisions.renal: none: common neurogenic bladder (~80-90%) is a separately diagnosed consequence of neural injury; direct urinary tract damage at >=30% is not established.

basis: Skeletal myopathy and defective protein O-glycosylation define this umbrella. Brain and eye abnormalities in severe congenital forms lack established >=30% frequencies across the full group.

decisions.neurologic: none: severe congenital dystroglycanopathy can affect the brain, but involvement in >=30% across this broader myopathy umbrella is not established.
decisions.ocular: none: ocular malformations occur in severe congenital forms; no supplied evidence establishes direct ocular damage in >=30% across the umbrella.

basis: Cerebellar and cardiac malformations are core 3C features; skeletal dysplasia and chorioretinal coloboma each occur in 2/2. Cardiac defect occurs in 1/2; samples are very small.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiac malformations are a core feature of the parent cranio-cerebello-cardiac syndrome; an atrioventricular canal defect is documented in 1/2.
decisions.ocular: involved: chorioretinal coloboma in 2/2 establishes common structural ocular involvement; microphthalmia is also documented in 1/2.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: distal phalangeal shortening and epiphyseal stippling each occur in 2/2, establishing common skeletal malformation.

basis: Axonal sensorimotor neuropathy with pyramidal involvement defines disease. Weakness in 20/20 and denervation-related wasting do not establish direct muscle pathology.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: weakness in 20/20 and distal wasting reflect denervation; common direct skeletal-muscle or joint damage is not established.

basis: Chronic lymphatic obstruction produces enlargement and fibrotic thickening of skin and subcutis. Lymphatics are outside the defined cardiovascular axis; infection is not universal.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: lymphatic obstruction does not establish disease of the heart, arteries, veins or blood capillaries covered by this axis.

basis: Urinary sulfate excess with low circulating sulfate supports renal sulfate wasting and disturbed sulfate homeostasis. Kidney stone in 1/1 is separately diagnosed and adds no organ.

decisions.renal: primary: urinary sulfate excess despite low circulating sulfate supports a renal sulfate-reabsorption disorder; the label does not depend on nephrolithiasis.
